# .github/workflows
- `staging.yml` — **the PR preview.** Every push to a PR into `main` that touches `worker/` applies the migrations to `memento-mori-staging` and deploys it — so a change can be checked from a phone before the PR is merged. One staging Worker: the last PR pushed wins. A **separate file from `ci.yml` on purpose**: the two need opposite concurrency policies, because CI cancels a superseded run and a deploy must never be cancelled between "migrations applied" and "Worker deployed". It does not run the tests (`ci.yml` does, on the same push) and does not `npm ci` (only wrangler runs). **Seeding is `npm run seed:staging` or `workflow_dispatch` + `reseed`, never automatic** — seeding on every push would wipe whatever you were half way through testing. **`workflow_dispatch` needs the workflow file on the DEFAULT branch** (`main`); `npm run seed:staging` is the path that always works.
- `ci.yml` — **The gate before main.** `npm test` on every pull request, then (into `main`) a check that a PR changing `worker/` also bumps the version — `main` must never hold code that is not live. No push trigger: the PR was tested, and `release.yml` tests again before it deploys. It exists because `npm test` otherwise ran only in the local push hook — which a cloud session's PR and a browser merge both miss — and in the release job, by which point the code is already on `main`. Deliberately ONE job: `test-api.js` already applies every migration and `worker/seed.sql` to a real SQLite database, so a `wrangler d1 migrations apply --local` step would download wrangler to re-prove that. `test` is the required check on `main`.
- `release.yml` — the only path to live; CLAUDE.md "Git workflow" has the order. The `backmerge` job is gone with `develop` (2026-10-03). Needs the repo secrets `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
